# A monetary number token in ordinary report formatting: optional ``$``/spaces,
# US thousands separators, and a decimal fraction. The boundaries reject a
# digit/comma/dot directly before and a digit directly after, so the match is
# never a substring of a larger number like ``1451.10`` for an expected
# ``451.10``.
_PRICE_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.,])\$?\s*\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d+)?(?!\d)")


def _normalize_number_token(token: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a matched number token (``$``/commas removed) into a Decimal."""
    cleaned = token.replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip()
input.newString:
# A monetary number token in ordinary report formatting: optional ``$``/spaces,
# an explicit sign, US thousands separators, and a decimal fraction. Ungrouped
# integers of any length match, correctly grouped comma amounts match, and the
# sign stays part of the numeric value so ``-451.10`` is never read as
# ``451.10``. The boundaries reject a digit/comma/dot directly before and a
# digit directly after, so the match is never a substring of a larger number
# like ``1451.10`` for an expected ``451.10``.
_PRICE_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![\d.,])\$?\s*[+-]?\s*(?:\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?!\d)"
)


def _normalize_number_token(token: str) -> Decimal | None:
    """Parse a matched number token (``$``/commas removed, sign kept) into a Decimal."""
    cleaned = token.replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip()

def test_price_token_normalizes_comma_thousands():
    """Comma thousands are ordinary formatting of the same number."""
    from research_desk.eval.live import _contains_price

    assert _contains_price("Priced at $1,234.56 per share.", 1234.56) is True
    assert _contains_price("Priced at $12,345.67.", 2345.67) is False
input.newString:
def test_price_token_normalizes_comma_thousands():
    """Comma thousands are ordinary formatting of the same number."""
    from research_desk.eval.live import _contains_price

    assert _contains_price("Priced at $1,234.56 per share.", 1234.56) is True
    assert _contains_price("Priced at $12,345.67.", 2345.67) is False


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "text,expected_close,should_match",
    [
        ("The close was 1234.50.", 1234.5, True),  # ungrouped integer of any length
        ("The close was $1,234.50.", 1234.5, True),  # correctly grouped comma amount
        ("The close was -451.10.", 451.1, False),  # sign is part of the value
        ("The close was 1451.10.", 451.1, False),  # substring of a larger number
    ],
)
def test_price_token_sign_and_grouping(text, expected_close, should_match):
    from research_desk.eval.live import _contains_price

    assert _contains_price(text, expected_close) is should_match
